_comment: Catalog shown by DemoBrowser.lua. One entry per demo, in browsing order. 'scene' must also be listed in assets/projects/TutorialsProject.json. Files, scripts, shaders and object counts are read from the scene JSON at runtime, so only describe the demo here.

demos.title: Lights imported from FBX
demos.summary: A scene whose point and spot lights come from a Blender/FBX file instead of being placed in the editor. The scene JSON only stores a lightsFile path; the lights are regenerated from the FBX on every load.
learn: lightsFile in the scene JSON -> SceneLoader::LoadLightsFileAssociation
Imported lights are not saved back into the scene file

demos.title: Show room
demos.summary: A small set of meshes and lights to look at the deferred renderer: G-Buffer, ADS lighting, shadows and a chromatic aberration post-processing shader on top.
learn: Post-processing shader stored in the scene shaders list

demos.title: Lights and day/night cycle
demos.summary: Point and spot lights plus a global (directional) light that a scene script rotates to simulate a 30 s day/night cycle, changing ambient and diffuse colours over time.

demos.title: Particle emitters
demos.summary: Sixteen particle emitters with different settings (speed, gravity, colours, lifetime) next to reference meshes. Every emitter is configured from the editor and saved in the scene.
learn: Emitter settings are part of the object JSON
Object Properties window (F10 in the editor) to tweak them live

demos.title: Performance test
demos.summary: Spawns objects in batches to stress the engine: static meshes, physics bodies, particle emitters, point lights or animated meshes, with an FPS readout.
controls: Left/Right  spawn rate      M / N  object cap
learn: ObjectFactory.* to create objects from Lua
Profiler window in the editor to see where the frame goes

demos.title: Rain of physics cubes
demos.summary: Three emitter objects run an object script that spawns a physics cube every half second. The cubes are Bullet rigid bodies that fall and pile up on the floor.
learn: Object script: RainCubesDemo.lua (this is the owner object)
Script variables (frequency) come from the JSON types file of the script

demos.title: Swarm (boids)
demos.summary: A Swarm object steering thirty meshes with the classic boids rules: separation, alignment and cohesion. The members are ordinary meshes referenced by the swarm.
learn: Swarm members are resolved after loading (ThreadJobResolveSwarms)

demos.title: Text rendering
demos.summary: Every way of drawing text: TTF auto-size, TTF with explicit size, batched glyph atlas, centred and aligned text, and cached text.
learn: Atlas text is the cheapest for HUDs that change every frame

demos.title: Post-processing chain
demos.summary: Eight full-screen shaders chained one after another, each tinting a different quarter of the screen. Shows how the ping-pong buffers pass the image from one shader to the next.
learn: Scene shaders run after the light pass (frame step 6)
UVs are screen space: gl_FragCoord.xy / textureSize
Shader node editor and code editor in the editor GUI

demos.title: Projectiles and collisions
demos.summary: A launcher fires physics projectiles; an object script logs on screen every collision it receives.

demos.title: UI widgets
demos.summary: The JSON widget system: a nested widget, a list widget and single cards drawn at a position, all fed with data from Lua every frame.
